feature.name: Cross-project dependency map
feature.description: Visualize blockers across teams with live links to tasks and Slack digests when critical paths slip.

executiveSummary: FlowStack's Cross-project dependency map targets B2B SaaS companies with 20-200 employees running multiple parallel initiatives, sold to a Head of Product or VP Engineering, with a 14-week build using 2 full-stack engineers, 30% of a PM, 3 designer weeks, and ~$3k/mo incremental graph/alerting infra at beta. The competitive set (Linear, Asana, monday.com, and the intended Jira/Atlassian comparison) is heavily capitalized and consolidating into AI work platforms: Linear raised an $82M Series C (2025-06-10) and a $99M secondary led by Accel (2026-08-26); Asana acquired Stack AI (2026-05-27) and has raised $453.2M in total disclosed funding across 12 rounds; monday.com acquired One AI (2026-05-11) and has raised $384.1M across 7 rounds. Linear is the sharpest direct threat: it has grown to 291 employees (+69.19% YoY) with 88 engineers (30.24%) and a sales org that grew from 9 (Dec 2024) to 29 (Aug 2026), evidencing an upmarket push that leaves the sub-200-employee, low-complexity segment comparatively underserved. No competitor description in the supplied data names a cross-project dependency visualization or Slack critical-path digest capability, which is the clearest whitespace signal available. However, the risk is bundling: Asana (4,428 employees, 902 in engineering) and monday.com (claimed 250,000+ customers and 60%+ of the Fortune 500) can absorb adjacent planning features into existing suites at near-zero incremental price. Two material evidence gaps constrain confidence: the 'Jira' competitor resolved to an unrelated 9-person training site (jiratutorials.com), so Atlassian — the default tool for engineering-centric squads — is entirely unassessed; and the jobs data returned empty plus a job_search tool error, so no hiring-demand validation exists. With ~22 months runway and negative EBITDA (~$180k/mo burn), the 14-week window is real but the feature should be scoped as a differentiated wedge (live task links + Slack digests on critical-path slips) rather than a general planning rebuild.

FlowStack should lead with the outcome incumbents do not advertise — Slack digests fired when a critical path slips — and keep live task links as the trust mechanism, rather than competing on graph rendering alone.

gapsAndOpportunities: No competitor in the supplied data publicly describes a cross-project dependency map with live task links and Slack digests on critical-path slips — the feature as specified is not advertised by Linear, Asana or monday.com.

Linear's combination of aggressive hiring (+69.19% YoY, 88 engineers) and a sales build-out (9 to 29) indicates an upmarket trajectory, plausibly opening the 20-200 employee, low-administration segment that FlowStack's target market and Alicia persona describe.
Asana's SF Bay Area contraction (1,021 to 829) and Poland expansion (142 to 205) signal enterprise-scale cost optimization rather than investment in lightweight mid-market coordination tooling.

Asana and monday.com are absorbing AI acquisitions (Stack AI, One AI) but neither acquisition is described as addressing cross-team dependency visibility — an integration seam FlowStack can occupy before they extend.

monday.com's claimed 250,000+ customers and 60%+ Fortune 500 penetration define a bundling threat but also validate budget existence for work-management software; FlowStack can sell the missing cross-team view alongside rather than replacing these suites.

Both Linear and Asana buy paid search against atlassian.com, indicating Atlassian is the category reference point for engineering-centric teams; Atlassian itself is unprofiled in this bundle, so its dependency-mapping posture is an open research question rather than a known gap.

FlowStack's economics allow a differentiated infra approach: ~$3k/mo incremental graph/alerting infra during beta against ~72% gross margin and ~$1.8M ARR, which is affordable only if the feature converts to pipeline within the 14-week window.
risks: Direct feature replication by Linear: fresh capital ($99,000,000 secondary, 2026-08-26), 88 engineers (30.24% of headcount) and +72 headcount in six months give it the capacity to ship a comparable dependency view inside FlowStack's 14-week build window.

Bundling by larger incumbents: Asana (4,428 employees, 902 engineers, 170,000+ claimed organizations) and monday.com (250,000+ claimed customers, 60%+ of Fortune 500) can fold dependency visibility into existing suites at near-zero incremental price, eroding FlowStack's ability to charge separately.

AI-platform consolidation: Asana's acquisition of Stack AI (2026-05-27) and monday.com's acquisition of One AI (2026-05-11) shift buyer criteria toward AI-driven planning; a deterministic dependency graph without AI framing may be judged feature-incomplete in evaluations.

Unassessed primary incumbent: the 'Jira' competitor resolved to an unrelated 9-person training site (crustdata_company_id 1259394, jiratutorials.com), so Atlassian — the default tool for the engineering-heavy squads in Elena's and Chris's scenarios — is entirely unanalyzed.

No demand-side evidence: rawBundle.jobs is empty and the job_search call errored, so there is no hiring-based validation that 20-200 employee B2B SaaS companies are creating the coordination roles that would buy this.

No product-level competitive intelligence: the bundle contains no competitor feature matrices, pricing, packaging or roadmap data, so the 'no one advertises this' finding cannot be converted into a defensible differentiation claim.

Competitor benchmark instability: monday.com's headcount series (4,564 -> 12,996 -> 5,914 around 2026-09) and Brazil concentration (7,099, 75.08% of reported total) are internally inconsistent, so any sizing of that competitor is unreliable.

Resource concentration and runway: 2 full-stack engineers out of a 7-person team for 14 weeks plus PM at 30% and 3 designer weeks, against ~$180k/mo burn, negative EBITDA, a 72% gross margin and 22 months of runway — a slip in the 14 weeks delays other roadmap work with no slack.

Monetization ceiling vs. effort: the stated financial threshold of $180,000 implies enterprise-flavored deal expectations, while the target segment (20-200 employees, 'without enterprise complexity') is typically lower-ACV and self-serve oriented — the pricing model is not evidenced in the data.

Channel dependency: the feature's differentiated promise rests on Slack digests, but no data in the bundle evidences Slack integration feasibility, rate limits, or buyer permission for automated cross-team alerting.

Evidence-base risk: personas and the new-install persona derive from flowstack-user-interviews-summary.pdf and dependency-map-spec-v2.pdf, neither of which is included in the raw bundle for verification.
dataLimitations: The 'Jira' competitor did not resolve to Atlassian. company_identify returned 'Jira Tutorial' (crustdata_company_id 1259394, jiratutorials.com, employee_count_range 'myself only', ~9 employees) as the top match, with null funding fields and empty competitor/SEO arrays. No Atlassian company profile, funding, headcount or product data is present in the bundle, so one of four named competitors is effectively unanalyzed.

Several function-level step changes (e.g., monday.com Sep-2025 jumps across Engineering, Marketing, Sales, HR, Finance, Accounting and Consulting; Asana's Sep-2025 jumps) are not explained by any event data in the bundle and are likely data-collection artifacts rather than real single-month hiring.

The competitor domain lists returned by company_enrich are noisy and include many unrelated companies (e.g., circleci.com, limewire.com, longnow.org under Linear; asanarecovery.com, hivyapp.com under Asana), so they were not used as competitor-identification evidence.

No interview transcripts, survey data, win/loss data, or pricing research were supplied, so all demand-side statements rest on the provided persona descriptions only.

Financial context for FlowStack (ARR ~$1.8M, 15% QoQ growth, ~72% gross margin, ~$180k/mo burn, 22 months runway) comes solely from productData.companyProfitabilityDetails and is unaudited in the bundle.
